title: Edges and counters
summary: An edge is the moment a signal changes. Counting events, reacting once per button press and detecting a part that arrives all depend on edges rather than on signal levels.

sections.heading: Level versus edge
sections.body: A **level** is the current value of a signal: the button is pressed. An **edge** is a change: the button has just been pressed (rising edge, FALSE to TRUE) or just released (falling edge, TRUE to FALSE). A rising edge is TRUE for exactly one scan.

sections.heading: Edge detection
sections.body: IEC 61131-3 provides **R_TRIG** (rising edge) and **F_TRIG** (falling edge). Each instance remembers the previous value of its input and compares it with the current one. Without edge detection, a held button would trigger an action in every scan, which is why a counter fed by a raw level counts once per scan instead of once per press.

sections.heading: Counters
sections.body:
- **CTU** counts up on each rising edge of CU and sets Q when the count reaches the preset PV. R resets the count.
- **CTD** counts down on each rising edge of CD; LD loads the preset and Q signals that zero was reached.
- **CTUD** combines both directions.

The standard counters detect the edge of their count input themselves, so a held button is counted once.

sections.heading: Signals faster than the scan
sections.body: A PLC sees inputs only once per scan. A pulse shorter than one scan can be missed completely, and two pulses within one scan count as one. Real controllers use hardware counter modules for fast signals; PLC Lab's fixed scan makes the effect visible in the timeline.
